column1: # Orbitals (Switch 2, v327680). Plays on the Mac: see README.md
# Unreal Engine 5.6.1, SDK 21.4.2 built for the Switch 2 (Ounce), NVN2 (Ampere shaders), Wwise 2024.1; modules main + subsdk0 (movie) + sdk. A two-player co-op game.
# Packed from a dump folder (no NACP in it, so the app takes the name below). Shaders: Unreal's IoStore shader libraries (ShaderArchive-*-SF_GLSL_SWITCH2), Oodle.
# Unreal: nninitStartup reserves a 62 GB address region and its FMallocBinned3 takes 37 GB of it, so a 64 GB alias region on the Mac. The rewriter cuts the allocator in any Unreal 4 / 5 main
# (dm/tools/ue_malloc.py) and gives the region what the alias region has room for (dm/tools/ue_region.py), as Octopath Traveler 0's profile (docs/reference/memory.md). In its first 15 s
# in nnMain the game's regions reach alias +63.00 GB (what it takes later in play is not measured)
# the NPDM declares 20 MB of system resource
# the decoded shader code archives: the engine's global shaders and the game's material shaders
# Unreal issues its own NVN barriers, so its passes order themselves: full barriers between passes serialised about 54 full-screen passes a frame at the character select (15 -> 18 fps there,
# no visual change). nvn_mtl.m barrier_game; DM_NVN_BARRIER overrides
# Metal encoding on its own thread: the game's frame is bound by the submitting thread (about 10,000 draws a frame in the 3D scenes)
# The game's own 30 fps: its config sets t.MaxFPS 30 and rhi.SyncInterval 2. The Switch 2 holds an even 30 here (a 60 fps capture of it: 173 of 182 frames 33.3 ms apart). With the cap
# at 30 the Mac (M4 Pro) gives 1198 of 1199 presents two refreshes apart; unlocked to 60 (the rewriter finds both variables by name, hle_fpslock.c) it gave 55-59 fps with missed vsyncs
